question:
Consider the system of equations
$$x+y+z=6$$
$$2x-y+3z=9$$
$$3x+2y-z=4$$

(a) Form the coefficient matrix $A$ and evaluate $|A|$.

(b) Examine the consistency of the system and state the number of solutions.

(c) Solve the system and verify the solution in the three equations.
explanation:
(a)
The coefficient matrix is
$$A=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 1\\2 & -1 & 3\\3 & 2 & -1\end{bmatrix}$$
Therefore,
$$|A|=\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 & 1\\2 & -1 & 3\\3 & 2 & -1\end{vmatrix}$$
Expanding along the first row,
$$|A|=1(1-6)-1(-2-9)+1(4+3)$$
$$|A|=-5+11+7=13$$

(b)
Since
$$|A|=13\neq0$$
the system is consistent and has a unique solution.

(c)
From the first equation,
$$x=6-y-z$$
Substituting in the second equation,
$$2(6-y-z)-y+3z=9$$
$$-3y+z=-3$$
$$z=3y-3$$
Substituting $x=6-y-z$ in the third equation,
$$3(6-y-z)+2y-z=4$$
$$y+4z=14$$
Using $z=3y-3$,
$$y+4(3y-3)=14$$
$$13y=26$$
$$y=2$$
Thus,
$$z=3(2)-3=3$$
and
$$x=6-2-3=1$$
Verification:
$$1+2+3=6$$
$$2(1)-2+3(3)=9$$
$$3(1)+2(2)-3=4$$
Hence, the unique solution is $(x,y,z)=(1,2,3)$.

options.A:
(a) $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&1&1\\2&-1&3\\3&2&-1\end{bmatrix}$, $|A|=-13$
(b) The system has a unique solution
(c) $(x,y,z)=(-1,2,5)$
options.B:
(a) $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&1&1\\2&-1&3\\3&2&-1\end{bmatrix}$, $|A|=0$
(b) The system has infinitely many solutions
(c) $(1,2,3)$ is one solution
options.C:
(a) $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&1&1\\2&-1&3\\3&2&-1\end{bmatrix}$, $|A|=13$
(b) The system is consistent and has a unique solution
(c) $(x,y,z)=(1,2,3)$, which satisfies all three equations
options.D:
(a) $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&1&1\\2&-1&3\\3&2&-1\end{bmatrix}$, $|A|=13$
(b) The system is inconsistent
(c) It has no solution
